CONTEXT — the bug being fixed:
Each app embeds RapidMeta.realData keyed by NCT with per-arm counts tE/tN (treatment events/N), cE/cN (comparator), plus a displayed ratio effect publishedHR (OR/RR/HR) with CI. An audit found that for 57/249 checkable binary trials (22.9%) the displayed arm counts implied the OPPOSITE direction to the displayed effect. Root cause (scripts/bulk_clone_audit_first.py + scripts/add_topic_autodiscover.py): the count selector (a) included AACT param_type='NUMBER' rows which are PERCENTAGES (a 17.3% responder rate became "17 events"), (b) took rows across ALL outcomes not the primary, (c) assigned treatment/comparator by sorting group ids so placebo (usually first) became "treatment". Counts and effect were sourced independently and never reconciled.

THE FIX (what to attack):
1. scripts/count_consistency.py — the invariant: counts must imply the same direction as the ratio effect, else counts must not be shown. Functions consistent() and orient_to_effect().
2. scripts/assert_count_effect_consistency.py — build gate, wired into bulk_clone ship path; BLOCKS any app whose counts contradict its effect. Run: python scripts/assert_count_effect_consistency.py (currently OK across 1448 files).
3. Corpus remediation (57 flagged + 9 more corpus-wide): 29 OR/RR trials RE-DERIVED from CT.gov v2 and 37 HR/time-to-event trials BLANKED (counts set null, publishedHR+CI kept). Re-derivation algorithm (scratchpad rederive_counts.py): find the CT.gov analysis whose measure+value matches the DISPLAYED effect within 12%; take its two groupIds; reconstruct events for those groups from the outcome measure (percentage*denom, or COUNT_OF_PARTICIPANTS); pick the arm orientation whose recomputed OR/RR reproduces the displayed effect value within 12%; if none matches, BLANK. Example: BRAVE-AA2 was tE4/tN173 cE19/cN174 (OR 7.86) -> now tE27/tN156 cE4/cN156 (recomputed OR 7.95).
4. Generator fix: extractors now scope count rows to the PRIMARY outcome and keep only COUNT_OF_PARTICIPANTS (drop NUMBER/percentage); generator reconciles counts to the effect at build (orient or blank); clone_dashboard renders None as JS null.

SPECIFIC ATTACK SURFACES I want you to probe:
A. The blank policy: for HR trials I ALWAYS blank counts (pooling uses CI-derived SE, unaffected). Is blanking ever hiding a real, correctly-derivable count? Is CANAGLIFLOZIN/CREDENCE (blanked because CT.gov reports an event-RATE not raw counts; the 245/340 lives only in the NEJM paper) the right call, or should it show 245/340?
B. The orient-to-effect logic: by choosing the arm orientation that reproduces the DISPLAYED effect, do I risk endorsing a WRONG displayed effect and making counts spuriously "consistent" with it? Where could that hide a real error?
C. The 12% magnitude tolerance and the direction neutral band (0.87-1.15): can a genuinely-wrong count pass these?
D. BARICITINIB BRAVE-AA2: the app displays OR 7.86 which is the 2mg-vs-placebo analysis (CT.gov also reports 4mg-vs-placebo OR 19.72). My fix set counts to the 2mg arm (17.3% -> 27/156). Is featuring the 2mg comparison instead of the pivotal 4mg a defect I have masked?
E. Same-direction magnitude errors: the gate only catches DIRECTION contradictions. A count that is wrong-magnitude but same-direction passes. How big is this residual and how would you detect it?

# sentinel:claim-language-allow
TITLE: MLM501: Cochrane Multilevel Meta-Analysis Effects Table from 501 Reviews
TYPE: methods  |  ESTIMAND: SMD
DATA: 501 Cochrane systematic reviews
PATH: C:\Projects\501MLM

CURRENT BODY (156 words):
Can a single R package unify effect-size data from hundreds of Cochrane reviews into a coherent multilevel meta-analysis effects table? We compiled 501 Cochrane systematic reviews covering dichotomous and continuous outcomes, preserving study-level moderators, DOI provenance, and original data URLs. MLM501 derives standardized treatment effects and standard errors, fits three-level random-effects models via metafor, and computes fragility indices using the MAFI algorithm for robustness. Across the 501-review corpus the pooled SMD was 0.24 (95% CI 0.18-0.31) with substantial review-level heterogeneity, and the median fragility index was 3, indicating most pooled conclusions depend on very few event reassignments. Leave-one-review-out analyses and robust variance estimation confirmed stability of the overall effect direction for both log-odds-ratio and standardized-mean-difference cohorts. A single importable table with full provenance enables rapid cross-review methods research without repeated manual extraction from the Cochrane archive. The package cannot address outcome definition heterogeneity across reviews, and users should exercise caution when pooling across clinically dissimilar interventions.

YOUR REWRITE (at most 156 words, 7 sentences):

Can a R package unify effect-size data from Cochrane reviews from 2023 onwards into a coherent multilevel meta-analysis effects table? We downloaded 501 Cochrane systematic reviews covering dichotomous and continuous outcomes while preserving study-level moderators. MLM501 derives standardized treatment effects and standard errors, fits three-level random-effects models via metafor, it computes fragility indices using the MAFI algorithm for robustness. Across corpus the pooled SMD was 0.24 (95% CI 0.18-0.31) (with substantial review-level heterogeneity). The median fragility index was 3, indicating most pooled conclusions depend on very few event reassignments. The Leave-one-review-out analyses and robust variance estimation confirmed stability of the overall effect direction for both log-odds-ratio and standardized-mean-difference cohorts. A single importable table with full provenance enables rapid cross-review methods research, the package cannot however address outcome definition heterogeneity across reviews.

[2/1873] 501MLM_Submission
TITLE: MLM501 Software Article: Building Large-Scale Meta-Analytic Datasets from Cochrane Reviews
TYPE: methods  |  ESTIMAND: OR
DATA: 501 Cochrane reviews, 12,847 study records
PATH: C:\Projects\501MLM_Submission

CURRENT BODY (156 words):
How can researchers efficiently construct large-scale multilevel meta-analysis datasets from Cochrane systematic reviews while preserving full data provenance? We developed MLM501 as an R package and applied it to 501 Cochrane reviews, extracting study-level effect sizes, moderators, and DOI-linked provenance metadata. The package automates effect-size derivation for dichotomous and continuous endpoints, fits three-level hierarchical models, computes fragility indices, and exports structured tables with audit trails. From 501 reviews the package assembled 12,847 study-level records with a pooled OR of 0.78 (95% CI 0.72-0.85) for the dichotomous cohort, confirming feasibility of automated large-scale construction. Cross-validation against manually extracted values from five benchmark reviews showed perfect concordance, and all unit tests passed across R versions 4.1 through 4.5. This tool reduces weeks of manual extraction to minutes, enabling methodological researchers to study cross-review heterogeneity patterns at scale. The current scope is limited to Cochrane reviews with downloadable data, and the importer cannot handle proprietary or non-standard review formats.

YOUR REWRITE (at most 156 words, 7 sentences):

Can we efficiently construct large-scale multilevel meta-analysis datasets from Cochrane systematic reviews with full data provenance? We created MLM501 as an R package and applied it to 501 Cochrane reviews, we extracted study-level effect sizes, moderators, and DOI-linked provenance metadata. The package automated effect-size derivation for dichotomous and continuous endpoints, fits three-level hierarchical models and computes fragility indices. From 501 reviews the package assembled 12,847 study-level records. The pooled OR was 0.78 (95% CI 0.72-0.85) for the dichotomous cohort, this confirms feasibility of automated large-scale construction. This tool reduces manual extraction enabling methodological researchers to study cross-review heterogeneity patterns at scale. However, current scope is limited to Cochrane reviews with downloadable data.

### hksj-q-floor-atlas (2026-05-12; 8th Pairwise70 atlas; tags prereg-v0.0.1 + v0.1.0)
> - `C:\Projects\hksj-q-floor-atlas\` â€” 8th calibration atlas in the Pairwise70 series. Sister to `cochrane-modern-re` (engine source), `repro-floor-atlas`, `responder-floor-atlas`, `trial-truthfulness-atlas`, `africa-tb-atlas`, `pactr-hiddenness-atlas`, `africa-hiv-prep-atlas`.
> - Question: how often does omitting the `max(1, Q/(k-1))` floor on HKSJ variance, in the I^2=0 regime where un-floored HKSJ narrows below REML+Wald, overstate precision across the Cochrane CDSR? Pre-registered via `prereg-v0.0.1` tag + 4 Internet Archive snapshots (Bitcoin OTS deferred â€” Python 3.13 SSL libeay32 bug per lessons.md; web-stamper fallback documented).
> - Headline: D_1 (I^2=0, k>=2, converged) = 3,677 MAs = 57.6% of corpus. On D_1a (Q>0, n=3,536): median CI-width ratio (floored / un-floored) = 3.64x (IQR 1.60-10.56; 95th pct 57.4x); significance lost in 17.08% of MAs. D_1b (Q=0, n=141 = 3.83% of D_1): sig_loss 24.8%, ratio unbounded â€” un-floored HKSJ SE is exactly zero (the floor effect is unbounded); see `docs/AMENDMENTS.md` entry 1 for split rationale.
> - Per k-stratum medians: k=2: 4.26x (sig_loss 8.6%); k=3: 3.64x (12.9%); k=4-5: 3.10x (13.1%); k=6-9: 3.18x (17.3%); k>=10: 3.80x (25.1%). sig_loss increases with k because higher-k pooled effects sit closer to null, so floor widening crosses zero more often.
> - Engine: independent metafor pass via fork of cochrane-modern-re's `run_metafor.R` minus the floor block. Input parquet SHA-256 pinned in `docs/spec.md` sec.1.5 (`31434fb118c6ec44a025eeb43a90e35ef9e050711fa45aa2cb5c1244b2d89751`). 3 hand-verified golden MAs match metafor reference within 1e-6.

 succeeded in 1873ms:
   1: """Shared count/effect consistency contract for RapidMeta.
   2: 
   3: Root-cause context (2026-07-12): the AACT results-table selector in
   4: `bulk_clone_audit_first.py` populated tE/cE from arbitrary outcome rows,
   5: independently of the separately-sourced effect estimate â€” it (a) included
   6: param_type='NUMBER' rows (AACT stores *percentages* that way, so a 17.3%
   7: responder rate became "17 events"), (b) flattened rows across *all* outcomes
   8: instead of the primary, and (c) assigned treatment/comparator by sorting the
   9: group ids, so placebo (usually the first group) was frequently labelled the
  10: treatment. The net effect: for ~23% of checkable binary trials the displayed
  11: arm counts implied the OPPOSITE direction to the plotted effect.
  12: 
  13: This module is the single source of truth for the invariant that closes the
  14: class: **a trial's displayed arm counts must imply the same direction as its
  15: displayed ratio effect, or the counts must not be shown.** It is imported by
  16: the generator (fail-safe at build) and by the standalone ship-gate.
  17: """
  18: from __future__ import annotations
  19: 
  20: # Neutral band: |RR-1| within this is "no direction" (matches the audit's
  21: # 0.87/1.15 tolerance used to measure the 57/249 baseline).
  22: _LO, _HI = 0.87, 1.15
  23: 
  24: 
  25: def _num(x):
  26:     try:
  27:         f = float(x)
  28:         return f if f == f else None  # drop NaN
  29:     except (TypeError, ValueError):
  30:         return None
  31: 
  32: 
  33: def implied_rr(tE, tN, cE, cN):
  34:     """Empirical risk ratio (tE/tN)/(cE/cN); None if not computable."""
  35:     tE, tN, cE, cN = _num(tE), _num(tN), _num(cE), _num(cN)
  36:     if None in (tE, tN, cE, cN):
  37:         return None
  38:     if tN <= 0 or cN <= 0 or cE <= 0 or tE <= 0:
  39:         return None
  40:     if tE > tN or cE > cN:
  41:         return None
  42:     return (tE / tN) / (cE / cN)
  43: 
  44: 
  45: def side(x, lo=_LO, hi=_HI):
  46:     """+1 (>1), -1 (<1), 0 (neutral band) â€” or None if x is None."""
  47:     if x is None:
  48:         return None
  49:     if x > hi:
  50:         return 1
  51:     if x < lo:
  52:         return -1
  53:     return 0
  54: 
  55: 
  56: def consistent(tE, tN, cE, cN, measure, effect):
  57:     """Is the counts-implied direction compatible with the effect direction?
  58: 
  59:     Returns:
  60:       True   â€” both sides defined and equal
  61:       False  â€” both sides defined and OPPOSITE (the trust-breaking case)
  62:       None   â€” undetermined (missing counts/effect, non-ratio measure, or either
  63:                side lands in the neutral band); callers treat None as "cannot
  64:                verify" â€” NOT as a pass.
  65:     Only ratio measures (OR/RR/HR/IRR) are checkable; MD/LSMD/continuous return
  66:     None.
  67:     """
  68:     if (measure or '').upper() not in ('OR', 'RR', 'HR', 'IRR'):
  69:         return None
  70:     eff = _num(effect)
  71:     if eff is None or eff <= 0:
  72:         return None
  73:     rr = implied_rr(tE, tN, cE, cN)
  74:     s_counts, s_eff = side(rr), side(eff)
  75:     if s_counts is None or s_eff is None or s_counts == 0 or s_eff == 0:
  76:         return None
  77:     return s_counts == s_eff
  78: 
  79: 
  80: def orient_to_effect(tE, tN, cE, cN, measure, effect):
  81:     """Return (tE,tN,cE,cN, status) where counts are oriented so their implied
  82:     direction matches the effect. status in {'ok','swapped','blank','asis'}.
  83: 
  84:     - If counts already consistent -> ('ok').
  85:     - If swapping arms makes them consistent -> ('swapped') with arms swapped.
  86:     - If neither orientation is consistent (or undetermined with a real effect
  87:       that has a direction) -> ('blank') with all four set to None.
  88:     - If the effect has no direction to check against -> ('asis') unchanged.
  89:     """
  90:     c = consistent(tE, tN, cE, cN, measure, effect)
  91:     if c is True:
  92:         return tE, tN, cE, cN, 'ok'
  93:     if c is False:
  94:         cS = consistent(cE, cN, tE, tN, measure, effect)
  95:         if cS is True:
  96:             return cE, cN, tE, tN, 'swapped'
  97:         return None, None, None, None, 'blank'
  98:     # c is None: if the effect itself has a direction but counts can't confirm,
  99:     # do NOT show a possibly-wrong table â€” blank. If the effect is non-ratio /
 100:     # directionless, leave as-is (nothing to contradict).
 101:     if (measure or '').upper() in ('OR', 'RR', 'HR', 'IRR') and side(_num(effect)) in (1, -1):
 102:         # counts missing or neutral: only blank when counts are actually present
 103:         if implied_rr(tE, tN, cE, cN) is not None:
 104:             return None, None, None, None, 'blank'
 105:     return tE, tN, cE, cN, 'asis'

   1: #!/usr/bin/env python
   2: """BUILD-TIME GATE: a shipped app must never display arm counts that contradict
   3: its displayed ratio effect. This is the structural fix for the count-provenance
   4: class (2026-07-12): the AACT row-selector sourced counts and effect independently
   5: and never reconciled them, so ~23% of checkable binary trials showed a table that
   6: implied the opposite of the plotted effect.
   7: 
   8: Scans one file, a list of files, or the whole corpus; exits non-zero (BLOCKS) if
   9: any trial's counts imply the opposite direction to its effect. Callable as a
  10: library (check_file / scan) or a CLI gate.
  11: 
  12: Usage:
  13:   python scripts/assert_count_effect_consistency.py                # whole repo
  14:   python scripts/assert_count_effect_consistency.py FILE ...        # given files
  15: """
  16: from __future__ import annotations
  17: import sys, io, os, re, glob
  18: sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
  19: import count_consistency as cc
  20: 
  21: # Reassign stdout only when run as a CLI. Doing it at import time corrupts
  22: # pytest's capture tmpfile (lessons.md: module-level sys.stdout reassignment).
  23: def _utf8_stdout():
  24:     if hasattr(sys.stdout, 'buffer') and getattr(sys.stdout, 'encoding', '').lower() != 'utf-8':
  25:         sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdout.buffer, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
  26: 
  27: ROOT = os.environ.get('RAPIDMETA_REPO_ROOT',
  28:                       os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
  29: _TRIAL = re.compile(r'"?(NCT\d{6,8})"?\s*:\s*\{')
  30: 
  31: def _objbody(s, i):
  32:     depth = 0; st = i
  33:     while i < len(s):
  34:         c = s[i]
  35:         if c == '{': depth += 1
  36:         elif c == '}':
  37:             depth -= 1
  38:             if depth == 0: return s[st:i+1]
  39:         i += 1
  40:     return s[st:]
  41: 
  42: def _num(o, k):
  43:     m = re.search(r'(?<![A-Za-z_])'+k+r':\s*(-?\d+\.?\d*|null)', o)
  44:     if not m: return None
  45:     return None if m.group(1) == 'null' else float(m.group(1))
  46: 
  47: def _sval(o, k):
  48:     m = re.search(k+r':"([^"]*)"', o)
  49:     return m.group(1) if m else None
  50: 
  51: def check_file(path):
  52:     """Return list of violation dicts for one app file."""
  53:     txt = open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
  54:     m = re.search(r'realData:\{', txt)
  55:     if not m: return []
  56:     body = _objbody(txt, m.end()-1)
  57:     viol = []
  58:     for tm in _TRIAL.finditer(body):
  59:         nct = tm.group(1)
  60:         o = _objbody(body, tm.end()-1)
  61:         tE, tN, cE, cN = _num(o,'tE'), _num(o,'tN'), _num(o,'cE'), _num(o,'cN')
  62:         pubHR = _num(o,'publishedHR')
  63:         est = _sval(o,'estimandType') or ('HR' if pubHR is not None else '')
  64:         # only checkable when we have full counts + a ratio effect
  65:         if None in (tE,tN,cE,cN,pubHR): continue
  66:         if cc.consistent(tE,tN,cE,cN, est or 'OR', pubHR) is False:
  67:             viol.append({'file': os.path.basename(path), 'nct': nct,
  68:                          'name': _sval(o,'name'), 'tE':tE,'tN':tN,'cE':cE,'cN':cN,
  69:                          'effect': pubHR, 'measure': est,
  70:                          'impliedRR': round(cc.implied_rr(tE,tN,cE,cN),3)})
  71:     return viol
  72: 
  73: def scan(paths):
  74:     all_v = []
  75:     for p in paths:
  76:         all_v.extend(check_file(p))
  77:     return all_v
  78: 
  79: def main(argv):
  80:     args = [a for a in argv[1:] if not a.startswith('-')]
  81:     if args:
  82:         paths = args
  83:     else:
  84:         paths = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, '*_REVIEW.html')))
  85:     viol = scan(paths)
  86:     checked = len(paths)
  87:     if viol:
  88:         print(f"[BLOCK] count/effect direction contradictions: {len(viol)} "
  89:               f"trial(s) in {len(set(v['file'] for v in viol))} app(s) "
  90:               f"across {checked} file(s) scanned")
  91:         for v in viol[:40]:
  92:             print(f"   {v['file']}  {v['nct']} {str(v['name'])[:14]:14} "
  93:                   f"tE{v['tE']:.0f}/{v['tN']:.0f} cE{v['cE']:.0f}/{v['cN']:.0f} "
  94:                   f"effect={v['effect']}({v['measure']}) impliedRR={v['impliedRR']}")
  95:         return 1
  96:     print(f"[OK] no count/effect contradictions across {checked} file(s) scanned")
  97:     return 0
  98: 
  99: if __name__ == '__main__':
 100:     _utf8_stdout()

   1: """Deterministic, self-verifying re-derivation of arm event counts from CT.gov v2.
   2: 
   3: Principle (non-circular): the displayed effect is the anchor. Find the CT.gov
   4: *analysis* whose measure+value matches the app's displayed effect, take its two
   5: compared groupIds, reconstruct events for exactly those two groups from the same
   6: outcome measure, then VERIFY the recomputed effect magnitude matches the reported
   7: one. Arm orientation is chosen by whichever orientation reproduces the reported
   8: effect value. If no analysis matches, or the outcome isn't a reconstructable
   9: participant proportion, or the magnitude can't be reproduced -> BLANK (keep the
  10: effect, drop the contradictory table).
  11: 
  12: Output: decisions.json  {app||nct: {action:'fix'|'blank', tE,tN,cE,cN, measure,
  13:  reported, recomputed, reason, out_title}}
  14: """
  15: import sys, io, os, json, re, math
  16: sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdout.buffer, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
  17: HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
  18: CACHE = os.path.join(HERE, 'ctgov_cache')
  19: 
  20: PARAM = {'hazard ratio':'HR','hazard ratio (hr)':'HR','risk ratio':'RR','risk ratio (rr)':'RR',
  21:          'relative risk':'RR','odds ratio':'OR','odds ratio (or)':'OR'}
  22: def norm_param(s):
  23:     if not s: return None
  24:     return PARAM.get(s.lower().strip())
  25: 
  26: COMPARATOR_RE = re.compile(r'placebo|control|standard|sham|comparator|usual care|best supportive|vehicle', re.I)
  27: 
  28: def is_percentage(om):
  29:     u = (om.get('unitOfMeasure') or '').lower()
  30:     return 'percent' in u or '%' in u
  31: def is_count(om):
  32:     u = (om.get('unitOfMeasure') or '').lower()
  33:     pt = (om.get('paramType') or '').upper()
  34:     return pt == 'COUNT_OF_PARTICIPANTS' or (u.strip() in ('participants','number of participants') and pt in ('NUMBER','COUNT_OF_PARTICIPANTS'))
  35: 
  36: def denom_for(om):
  37:     """Return {groupId: N} using the Participants denom block (prefer)."""
  38:     best = {}
  39:     for den in om.get('denoms', []):
  40:         units = (den.get('units') or '').lower()
  41:         m = {c.get('groupId'): _f(c.get('value')) for c in den.get('counts', [])}
  42:         if 'participant' in units:
  43:             return {k:v for k,v in m.items() if v is not None}
  44:         if not best:
  45:             best = {k:v for k,v in m.items() if v is not None}
  46:     return best
  47: 
  48: def _f(x):
  49:     try: return float(x)
  50:     except (TypeError, ValueError): return None
  51: 
  52: def measurement_map(om):
  53:     """Return list of (category_title, {groupId: value}) across classes/categories."""
  54:     rows = []
  55:     for cl in om.get('classes', []):
  56:         for cat in cl.get('categories', []):
  57:             mm = {m.get('groupId'): _f(m.get('value')) for m in cat.get('measurements', [])}
  58:             rows.append(((cat.get('title') or cl.get('title') or ''), mm))
  59:     return rows
  60: 
  61: def effect_from_2x2(est, e1, n1, e2, n2):
  62:     """effect of group1 vs group2 (group2 = reference)."""
  63:     if None in (e1,n1,e2,n2) or n1<=0 or n2<=0: return None
  64:     if est == 'RR':
  65:         if e2 == 0 or e1 == 0: return None
  66:         return (e1/n1)/(e2/n2)
  67:     # OR (and HR approximated by OR only as a last resort â€” we do NOT do that)
  68:     a,b,c,d = e1, n1-e1, e2, n2-e2
  69:     if min(a,b,c,d) <= 0: return None
  70:     return (a*b_inv(b))*(d)/c if False else (a/b)/(c/d)
  71: def b_inv(x): return 1.0/x
  72: 
  73: def close(a, b, tol=0.12):
  74:     if a is None or b is None or b == 0: return False
  75:     return abs(a-b)/abs(b) <= tol
  76: 
  77: def rederive(nct, est, reported):
  78:     """Return dict decision for one (nct, est, reported-effect-value)."""
  79:     fp = os.path.join(CACHE, f'{nct}.json')
  80:     if not os.path.exists(fp):
  81:         return {'action':'blank','reason':'no ctgov cache'}
  82:     d = json.load(open(fp, encoding='utf-8'))
  83:     if d.get('error'):
  84:         return {'action':'blank','reason':'ctgov error '+str(d['error'])}
  85:     oms = d.get('resultsSection',{}).get('outcomeMeasuresModule',{}).get('outcomeMeasures',[])
  86:     # gather candidate analyses matching measure + value
  87:     cands = []
  88:     for oi, om in enumerate(oms):
  89:         for a in om.get('analyses', []):
  90:             p = norm_param(a.get('paramType'))
  91:             if p != est: continue
  92:             val = _f(a.get('paramValue'))
  93:             if val is None: continue
  94:             gids = a.get('groupIds', [])
  95:             if len(gids) < 2: continue
  96:             score = abs(val-reported)/abs(reported) if reported else 9
  97:             cands.append((score, oi, om, a, val, gids))
  98:     cands.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
  99:     # only OR/RR are reconstructable from proportions
 100:     if est in ('OR','RR'):
 101:         for score, oi, om, a, val, gids in cands:
 102:             if score > 0.12:  # analysis value must match the displayed effect
 103:                 continue
 104:             g_ref, g_trt = gids[0], gids[1]   # CT.gov convention: first = reference/comparator
 105:             den = denom_for(om)
 106:             rows = measurement_map(om)
 107:             # choose the measurement row: prefer single category; else the row where both groups present
 108:             row = None
 109:             if len(rows) == 1:
 110:                 row = rows[0][1]
 111:             else:
 112:                 for title, mm in rows:
 113:                     if g_ref in mm and g_trt in mm and mm[g_ref] is not None and mm[g_trt] is not None:
 114:                         row = mm; break
 115:             if not row: continue
 116:             def events(g):
 117:                 v = row.get(g); N = den.get(g)
 118:                 if v is None or N is None: return (None, None)
 119:                 if is_percentage(om): return (round(v/100.0*N), int(N))
 120:                 if is_count(om):      return (int(round(v)), int(N))
 121:                 return (None, None)
 122:             e_trt, n_trt = events(g_trt)
 123:             e_ref, n_ref = events(g_ref)
 124:             if None in (e_trt, n_trt, e_ref, n_ref): continue
 125:             if not (0 <= e_trt <= n_trt and 0 <= e_ref <= n_ref): continue
 126:             # orient: try trt-vs-ref and ref-vs-trt, keep the one matching reported value
 127:             eff_a = effect_from_2x2(est, e_trt, n_trt, e_ref, n_ref)
 128:             eff_b = effect_from_2x2(est, e_ref, n_ref, e_trt, n_trt)
 129:             pick = None
 130:             if close(eff_a, reported): pick = ('A', e_trt,n_trt,e_ref,n_ref, eff_a)
 131:             elif close(eff_b, reported): pick = ('B', e_ref,n_ref,e_trt,n_trt, eff_b)
 132:             if not pick: continue
 133:             _, tE,tN,cE,cN, recomputed = pick
 134:             gtrt_title = next((g.get('title') for g in om.get('groups',[]) if g.get('id')==(g_trt if pick[0]=='A' else g_ref)), '')
 135:             gref_title = next((g.get('title') for g in om.get('groups',[]) if g.get('id')==(g_ref if pick[0]=='A' else g_trt)), '')
 136:             return {'action':'fix','tE':tE,'tN':tN,'cE':cE,'cN':cN,'measure':est,
 137:                     'reported':reported,'recomputed':round(recomputed,3),
 138:                     'out_title':(om.get('title') or '')[:120],
 139:                     'trt_group':gtrt_title,'ref_group':gref_title,
 140:                     'reason':f'matched analysis {est}={val} to reported {reported}; reconstructed from '
 141:                              +('percentage' if is_percentage(om) else 'count')}
 142:         return {'action':'blank','reason':f'no reconstructable OR/RR analysis matched reported {reported} within 12%'}
 143:     # HR (time-to-event): a 2x2 proportion cannot reproduce an HR value, but if
 144:     # CT.gov reports the PRIMARY event as a genuine participant COUNT for the two
 145:     # HR-analysis arms, those raw counts are real and their RR direction must
 146:     # agree with the HR. Use them (display-only; pooling still uses HR+CI). Else
 147:     # blank â€” we never transcribe a publication-only count the registry lacks.
 148:     # HR default: BLANK. A 2x2 proportion cannot reproduce an HR value, and
 149:     # orienting real arm counts to the HR direction risks endorsing a wrong
 150:     # effect. Trust mandate: no-number beats maybe-wrong-number. We keep HR+CI
 151:     # (which drives pooling and display) and drop the contradictory 2x2.
 152:     # HR-count reconstruction is retained below but GATED OFF by default.
 153:     HR_COUNT_ENABLED = False
 154:     if est == 'HR' and HR_COUNT_ENABLED:
 155:         for score, oi, om, a, val, gids in cands:
 156:             if score > 0.12: continue
 157:             if not is_count(om):   # rate-per-PY / median / KM% are NOT raw counts
 158:                 continue
 159:             g_ref, g_trt = gids[0], gids[1]
 160:             den = denom_for(om)
 161:             rows = measurement_map(om)
 162:             row = rows[0][1] if len(rows)==1 else None
 163:             if row is None:
 164:                 for title, mm in rows:
 165:                     if g_ref in mm and g_trt in mm and mm[g_ref] is not None and mm[g_trt] is not None:
 166:                         row = mm; break
 167:             if not row: continue
 168:             def cnt(g):
 169:                 v = row.get(g); N = den.get(g)
 170:                 if v is None or N is None: return (None,None)
 171:                 return (int(round(v)), int(N))
 172:             e_trt,n_trt = cnt(g_trt); e_ref,n_ref = cnt(g_ref)
 173:             if None in (e_trt,n_trt,e_ref,n_ref): continue
 174:             if not (0 <= e_trt <= n_trt and 0 <= e_ref <= n_ref): continue
 175:             if e_trt==0 or e_ref==0: continue
 176:             rr = (e_trt/n_trt)/(e_ref/n_ref)
 177:             def side(x): return 1 if x>1.02 else (-1 if x<0.98 else 0)
 178:             # HR<1 => treatment fewer events => RR should be <1 with trt as treatment
 179:             if side(rr)==side(reported) and side(reported)!=0:
 180:                 return {'action':'fix','tE':e_trt,'tN':n_trt,'cE':e_ref,'cN':n_ref,'measure':'HR',
 181:                         'reported':reported,'recomputed':round(rr,3),
 182:                         'out_title':(om.get('title') or '')[:120],
 183:                         'trt_group':next((g.get('title') for g in om.get('groups',[]) if g.get('id')==g_trt),''),
 184:                         'ref_group':next((g.get('title') for g in om.get('groups',[]) if g.get('id')==g_ref),''),
 185:                         'reason':f'HR trial with genuine participant COUNT outcome; RR={round(rr,3)} agrees with HR={reported} direction'}
 186:             # try swapped orientation
 187:             rr2 = (e_ref/n_ref)/(e_trt/n_trt)
 188:             if side(rr2)==side(reported) and side(reported)!=0:
 189:                 return {'action':'fix','tE':e_ref,'tN':n_ref,'cE':e_trt,'cN':n_trt,'measure':'HR',
 190:                         'reported':reported,'recomputed':round(rr2,3),
 191:                         'out_title':(om.get('title') or '')[:120],
 192:                         'trt_group':next((g.get('title') for g in om.get('groups',[]) if g.get('id')==g_ref),''),
 193:                         'ref_group':next((g.get('title') for g in om.get('groups',[]) if g.get('id')==g_trt),''),
 194:                         'reason':f'HR trial, genuine COUNT outcome, arm-oriented to HR direction; RR={round(rr2,3)}'}
 195:     if est == 'HR':
 196:         return {'action':'blank','reason':'HR/time-to-event: 2x2 counts cannot reproduce an HR; keep HR+CI only (pooling unaffected)'}
 197:     return {'action':'blank','reason':'unhandled measure'}
 198: 
 199: if __name__ == '__main__':
 200:     flags = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE,'baseline_flags.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
 201:     out = {}
 202:     nfix = nblank = 0
 203:     for app,nct,name,tE,tN,cE,cN,pubHR,est,emp in flags:
 204:         dec = rederive(nct, est, pubHR)
 205:         out[f'{app}||{nct}'] = dec
 206:         if dec['action']=='fix': nfix+=1
 207:         else: nblank+=1
 208:     json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(HERE,'decisions.json'),'w'), indent=1)
 209:     print(f'decisions: fix={nfix} blank={nblank} total={len(flags)}')
 210:     print('\n=== FIX decisions ===')
 211:     for k,v in out.items():
 212:         if v['action']=='fix':
 213:             print(f"{k[:52]:52} tE{v['tE']}/{v['tN']} cE{v['cE']}/{v['cN']} rep={v['reported']} recomp={v['recomputed']}  [{v['measure']}]")
 214:     print('\n=== BLANK decisions ===')
 215:     for k,v in out.items():
 216:         if v['action']=='blank':
 217:             print(f"{k[:52]:52} {v['reason'][:80]}")

   2: """Portfolio-wide data-integrity audit for the RapidMeta review apps.
   3: 
   4: Parses the realData trial objects out of every *_REVIEW*.html and runs a set of

   6: they apply to all topics. These encode the defect CLASSES uncovered in review so
   7: the rest of the portfolio can be checked for the same mistakes:
   8: 
   9:   impossible_2x2     tE>tN or cE>cN (event count exceeds arm size) -- the prior
  10:                      systemic extraction bug (154 apps) made concrete and gated.

  13:                      ReferenceError class fixed in NINTEDANIB/ZIRCONIUM.
  14:   inverted_ci        lci > uci on the published HR or an outcome.
  15:   ci_excludes_point  publishedHR not within [hrLCI, hrUCI] (1% slack).
  16:   implausible_ratio  a ratio estimand (HR/OR/RR) that is <=0, or so large the

  18:                      ratio (the DME Protocol-T 11.6 case).

  52: # JS number, or a corrupted/None token we want to catch. ORDER MATTERS: the
  53: # corruption token `nulle<digits>` (e.g. `tN:nulle4`, a `null` fused with an
  54: # exponent) MUST precede the plain `null` alternative, or the engine grabs `null`
  55: # first and never sees the `e4` -> the corruption is silently classified valid.
  56: # `nulle` requires the literal `e` so it never clashes with the benign minified

  61: def _match_brace(s: str, open_idx: int):
  62:     """Given index of a '{', return index of its matching '}' (string-aware)."""
  63:     depth = 0
  64:     in_str = None
  65:     esc = False
  66:     j = open_idx
  67:     n = len(s)
  68:     while j < n:
  69:         c = s[j]
  70:         if in_str:
  71:             if esc:
  72:                 esc = False
  73:             elif c == "\\":
  74:                 esc = True
  75:             elif c == in_str:
  76:                 in_str = None
  77:         else:
  78:             if c in "\"'":
  79:                 in_str = c
  80:             elif c == "{":
  81:                 depth += 1
  82:             elif c == "}":
  83:                 depth -= 1
  84:                 if depth == 0:
  85:                     return j
  86:         j += 1

rows=[]
for p in files:
    html=open(p,encoding='utf-8',errors='replace').read()
    for nct,obj in dia.find_trial_objects(html):
        vals={k:dia.as_num(dia.field(obj,k)) for k in ('tE','tN','cE','cN','publishedHR')}
        if any(vals[k] is None for k in ('tE','tN','cE','cN','publishedHR')): continue
        tE,tN,cE,cN,eff=(vals[k] for k in ('tE','tN','cE','cN','publishedHR'))
        if tN<=0 or cN<=0 or eff<=0: continue
        tail=obj.split('allOutcomes',1)
        m=None
        import re
        if len(tail)>1:
            mm=re.search(r'estimandType:\"(["'^"]+)"'"', tail[1]); m=mm.group(1) if mm else None
        est=(m or 'HR').upper()
        if est not in ('OR','RR','HR','IRR'): continue
        if not (tE==0 or cE==0 or tE==tN or cE==cN): continue
        # Haldane-Anscombe continuity for direction only
        a,b,c,d=tE,tN-tE,cE,cN-cE
        aa,bb,ccell,dd=a,b,c,d
        if min(aa,bb,ccell,dd)<=0:
            aa,bb,ccell,dd=aa+0.5,bb+0.5,ccell+0.5,dd+0.5
        rr=(aa/(aa+bb))/(ccell/(ccell+dd)) if ccell>0 else None
        odds=(aa/bb)/(ccell/dd) if bb>0 and ccell>0 and dd>0 else None
        s_eff=1 if eff>1.15 else (-1 if eff<0.87 else 0)
        s_rr=1 if rr and rr>1.15 else (-1 if rr and rr<0.87 else 0)
        s_or=1 if odds and odds>1.15 else (-1 if odds and odds<0.87 else 0)
        gate=cc.consistent(tE,tN,cE,cN,est,eff)
        if s_eff and (s_rr == -s_eff or s_or == -s_eff):
            rows.append((p,nct,est,tE,tN,cE,cN,eff,round(rr,3) if rr else None,round(odds,3) if odds else None,gate))
print('files',len(files),'zero/boundary opposite rows',len(rows))

            rows.append((rel,p,nct,nm.group(1) if nm else '',est,tE,tN,cE,cN,eff,calc,rr,or_,title[:80]))

codex
**Strongest objection**

The invariant is false for zero-cell and boundary-cell trials. `scripts/count_consistency.py:38-39` makes `implied_rr()` return `None` whenever `tE <= 0` or `cE <= 0`; `consistent()` then returns `None`, and `scripts/assert_count_effect_consistency.py:66` only blocks `False`. Worse, `orient_to_effect()` only blanks undetermined counts when `implied_rr(...) is not None` at `scripts/count_consistency.py:101-104`, so zero-cell contradictions survive as `asis`.

Concrete corpus failures that the gate says are OK:

```text
python scripts/assert_count_effect_consistency.py BIMEKIZUMAB_AXIAL_AUTO_FULL_REVIEW.html IXEKIZUMAB_AXIAL_AUTO_FULL_REVIEW.html ...
[OK] no count/effect contradictions across 6 file(s) scanned
```

But these are still direction-wrong under a standard 0.5 continuity correction:

```text
BIMEKIZUMAB_AXIAL_AUTO_FULL_REVIEW.html  NCT03928743  BE MOBILE 2
displayed OR=2.88, counts 0/111 vs 7/221
corrected RR=0.132, OR=0.128

IXEKIZUMAB_AXIAL_AUTO_FULL_REVIEW.html  NCT02696798  COAST-W
displayed OR=2.41, counts 0/104 vs 2/114
corrected RR=0.219, OR=0.215
```

That directly breaks the stated rule: counts are shown, the displayed effect is >1, but the displayed counts imply <1. The build gate certifies them because “zero” is treated as unverifiable instead of dangerous.

**Other objections**

The “always blank HR counts” policy is not implemented. `scripts/bulk_clone_audit_first.py:200-203` sends `HR` through `orient_to_effect()` just like `OR/RR/IRR`; there is no HR blank branch. I found 379 HR rows with non-null displayed counts in the top-level 1448 files. CREDENCE being blank is defensible if registry-only provenance is the rule, but the policy is not global or enforced.

Same-direction magnitude errors remain large. In 630 computable OR/RR rows with counts, I found 89 where the declared estimand magnitude differs by >12% while direction still agrees. Examples:

```text
FILGOTINIB_RA_AUTO_FULL_REVIEW.html  NCT02889796
declared OR=1.54, counts 364/475 vs 237/475
RR=1.54, OR=3.29

MPOX_VACCINE_NMA_REVIEW.html  NCT05480488
declared OR=18.7, counts 280/300 vs 15/300
RR=18.7, OR=266

HEPATITIS_HCV_DAA_REVIEW.html  NCT02201940
declared OR=99, counts 619/624 vs 0/116
corrected RR=232, corrected OR≈26,200
```

This is the wrong-but-looks-right class: direction passes, but the displayed label/value pair is not reproduced by the displayed counts.

The re-derivation is circular around the displayed effect. `scratchpad/rederive_counts.py:3-9` explicitly anchors on the app’s current effect, then `:126-131` chooses the arm orientation that reproduces it. If the displayed effect is the wrong comparison or wrong estimand, the procedure can make bad data internally coherent.

BRAVE-AA2 is exactly that risk. The fix made the counts match the displayed 2 mg OR 7.86. If the review question is “baricitinib for alopecia” and the clinically pivotal comparison is 4 mg vs placebo, this masks a comparison-selection error. The invariant proves only “counts match the chosen displayed effect,” not “the displayed effect is the right trial comparison.”

The ship gate is also narrower than “corpus-wide”: `assert_count_effect_consistency.py:84` defaults to `ROOT/*_REVIEW.html`. The repo contains subdirectory review pages too, so “OK across 1448 files” is not a recursive repo guarantee.
